impact:
T-006 made every ccusage payload fail loud on a producer schema change — except `blocks`.

`src/ccusage.ts:88-92` returns `runCcusage(ctx, args)` for `blocks --json` with no validator, and `tests-ts/contract/schema.contract.mjs` never invokes `blocks`, so the real-binary contract test — described in its own header as "the gate that makes a ccusage version bump safe" — does not cover it. A `blocks` schema change would pass that gate undetected.

Harmless TODAY: no TS consumer reads the payload yet (`cmd_blocks` is not ported), so there is nothing to mis-aggregate. The exposure arrives with T-004, which ports the renderers. Note `usage.py:590` reads `b.get("costUSD", b.get("totalCost", 0))`, i.e. it silently zeroes in BOTH languages — so porting `cmd_blocks` without a validator would reopen exactly the hole T-006 closed everywhere else, and the `costUSD`/`totalCost` fallback means a rename of EITHER key is invisible.

Recommended when T-004 ports `cmd_blocks`: add `validateBlocks` following the same rule the other validators follow (validate only what the downstream would otherwise accept silently — see the header of src/json.ts), and add a `blocks` case to the real-binary contract test.

Found by code review round 4.
title: `blocks --json` is the one ccusage payload with no schema validation or contract coverage
